fi-microspathodon-chrysurus.title: Atlantic Jewel Damsel
fi-microspathodon-chrysurus.summary: A Caribbean damsel with sparkling blue dots when young; adults turn brown to yellow with faint spots.
rows: About 6 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 21 cm (8.3 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep only one per tank; it is very aggressive
Omnivore. Meaty foods, herbivore preparations and flake
Western Atlantic: southern Florida (USA) and Bermuda through the Caribbean Sea to Brazil
notes: Juveniles in the wild shelter in fire coral (Millepora).

fi-dascyllus-trimaculatus.title: Domino Damsel
fi-dascyllus-trimaculatus.summary: A black damsel with three white spots that fade with age. Very hardy but becomes aggressive as it matures.
rows: About 5½ in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Omnivore. Meaty foods, herbivore preparations and flake
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to the Line and Pitcairn islands, north to southern Japan, south to Sydney, Australia
notes: May host in a carpet anemone (Stichodactyla) if one is present.
Tolerates less-than-perfect water, which is why it is often a first fish.

fi-chromis-viridis.title: Green Chromis
fi-chromis-viridis.summary: A peaceful blue-green damsel that schools over branching corals. Very hardy and reef safe.
rows: About 4 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 10 cm (3.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep a school of at least six
Omnivore. Several small feedings a day of meaty foods, herbivore flakes and frozen foods
Indo-Pacific: East coast of Africa to the Line Islands and Tuamotu Archipelago; north to Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef and New Caledonia
notes: Gets along with almost all community fish, invertebrates and corals.
Can live 8–15 years with excellent water quality.

fi-pomacentrus-smithi.title: Pink Damsel
fi-pomacentrus-smithi.summary: Smith's Damsel: a small silvery damsel edged in pink. Hardy and reef safe.
rows: About 2.75 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 7 cm (2.8 in) TL (FishBase)
A small group works if there are enough rocks to break up territories
Omnivore. Frozen brine and mysis shrimp, dried seaweed and flake
Western Central Pacific: Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and New Hebrides

fi-dascyllus-aruanus.title: Three Stripe Damsel
fi-dascyllus-aruanus.summary: The Humbug Dascyllus: bold black and white bands. Very hardy but aggressive as an adult.
rows: About 3¾ in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 10 cm (3.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Omnivore. Meaty items, herbivore preparations and flake
Pacific Ocean: region north and east of Lombok Strait to Line, Marquesan and Tuamoto islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia
notes: Does not harm invertebrates or rearrange the tank.
warn: Aggressive adult; best with other moderately aggressive fish.

fi-amblyglyphidodon-aureus.title: Yellow Damsel
fi-amblyglyphidodon-aureus.summary: A golden-yellow damsel, sometimes with blue lines when young. Hardy and reef safe; color fades and aggression rises with age.
rows: About 3 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 13 cm (5.1 in) TL (FishBase)
Omnivore. Meaty foods and herbivore preparations
Western Pacific: Andaman Sea and Christmas Island in the eastern Indian Ocean to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands
notes: Handles a wide range of tank conditions.

fi-chrysiptera-parasema.title: Yellowtail Blue Damsel
fi-chrysiptera-parasema.summary: A jewel-blue damsel with a yellow tail. One of the gentler damsels, and it fits smaller tanks.
rows: About 2¾ in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 7 cm (2.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Omnivore. Small meaty foods, herbivore foods and flake
Western Pacific: including Solomon Islands, northern Papua New Guinea, Philippines, and Ryukyu Islands
notes: Likes multiple hiding places and peaceful tankmates.

fi-chrysiptera-cyanea.title: Blue Damsel
fi-chrysiptera-cyanea.summary: A bright blue, hardy damsel that defends a small territory. Can darken almost to black when hiding.
rows: About 3 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 8.5 cm (3.3 in) TL (FishBase)
Somewhat aggressive. With other damsels, add many hiding places to break up territories
Omnivore. Flake, frozen foods and herbivore preparations
Indo-West Pacific: eastern edge of the Indian Ocean and Western Australia to New Guinea, New Britain, Solomon Islands, Marianas and Caroline Islands, Indonesia
notes: Good beginner fish and safe with invertebrates.
